skills.name: Practical: location of economic activities and land use

note.text: A site decision needs evidence about suitability, access and competing land uses. A map can show constraints, but its legend and date determine what can be concluded. In this guided practical, classify each plot against all the given rules, reject unsuitable plots with a reason and record the eligible choice. Real site approval requires further information and authorised decisions.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to read a site map and justify a choice against every stated criterion. Builds on: industrial location and competing land uses. Leads to: communication networks and route decisions.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: The invented map marks available land, a school reserve, a flood zone and road access. Our classroom rules require available land outside the marked flood zone with road access. In this example Plot A passes; B is reserved, C is flood-marked and D lacks access. The rules and hazard boundary are teaching inventions, not a survey of a real town.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Draw a record with plot, land status, flood status, access and decision. Read every label; do not choose from colour alone. State a rejection reason for each alternative, then name a real-world uncertainty such as soil, seasonal flooding or community needs.

information about a possible damaging process
a stated requirement for connection to transport
a comparison showing how each option meets the criteria

cards.idea: Distinguish the features before applying them.
example: land-use constraint: a competing or reserved use limiting a proposal.
hazard evidence: information about a possible damaging process.
access criterion: a stated requirement for connection to transport.
decision record: a comparison showing how each option meets the criteria.

cards.idea: Use the evidence in the example, not a place name alone.
example: The invented map marks a plot as a school reserve.
A plot lies in the map’s marked flood zone.
A plot has the required road connection.

right.text: land-use constraint: a competing or reserved use limiting a proposal.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: A competing designated use can rule out a classroom candidate. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: hazard evidence: information about a possible damaging process.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Road access does not remove a separate flood constraint. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: access criterion: a stated requirement for connection to transport.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Access is only one of the stated criteria. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

right.text: decision record: a comparison showing how each option meets the criteria.
right.explain: This distinction is correct: Recording each criterion makes the choice checkable. Look for a claim that reverses the process or makes an unsupported generalisation.

wrong.text: A reserved site is automatically available for a factory.
wrong.explain: A competing designated use can rule out a classroom candidate.

wrong.text: Any plot close to a road is free of flood risk.
wrong.explain: Road access does not remove a separate flood constraint.

wrong.text: Access alone satisfies every site rule.
wrong.explain: Access is only one of the stated criteria.

wrong.text: A decision requires no explanation of rejected options.
wrong.explain: Recording each criterion makes the choice checkable.
